findings.description: The trigger says execution is longer than the configured limit, but detection is required when the limit expires. At expiry the execution time equals the limit, so the boundary and detection instant are ambiguous. CON-SUP-103 uses both formulations.
findings.requested_change: Resolve the boundary condition and detection instant with the product owner, and state a consistent rule.

findings.description: CON-SUP-104 requires the checkpoint of every task released in a control cycle by that cycle's end, while CON-SUP-103 permits T_DIAG to execute for up to 20 ms in a 10 ms control cycle. The checkpoint's position within task execution is unspecified, so a permitted T_DIAG execution may be treated as a flow fault.
findings.requested_change: Resolve the checkpoint timing and cycle rule for T_DIAG with the product owner, then state a consistent, testable condition.

findings.description: The requirement permits watchdog refresh only while every supervised task is healthy, but neither the item nor its cited sources defines when a task is considered healthy, including before its first completion or after a detected fault.
findings.requested_change: Define the observable health condition governing refresh, including startup and fault behavior, using an agreed source.

findings.description: The requirement permits watchdog refresh only while every supervised task is healthy, but neither the item nor its cited sources defines when a task is considered healthy, including before its first completion or after a detected fault.
findings.requested_change: Define the observable health condition governing refresh, including startup and fault behavior, using an agreed source.

findings.description: The requirement specifies a CRC-32 check of the application image, but CON-SUP-107 specifies a stored CRC-32 only for the configuration block; it does not specify the application-image check algorithm or its reference value.
findings.requested_change: Obtain and record the agreed application-image integrity method and reference data, or remove the unsupported CRC-32 specification and record the missing decision.

findings.description: CON-SUP-107 supplies a CRC-32 polynomial, but neither it nor the requirement specifies the other parameters needed to reproduce the stored CRC, such as initialization, reflection and final XOR. A verifier cannot determine a unique expected result.
findings.requested_change: Obtain and reference a complete CRC definition, including its parameters and configuration-block coverage.

findings.description: The requirement directs the status signal high whenever startup checks have passed and no fault is present. CON-SUP-110 and SYS-SUP-027 require the safe state to remain latched until power-on after repeated faults, including across software and watchdog resets.
findings.requested_change: Include the safe-state latch in the conditions governing the operational status signal.

findings.description: CON-SUP-112 requires a fault report within 10 ms of detection, while CON-SUP-110 requires transmission after entering the safe state and SYS-SUP-022 and SYS-SUP-023 allow up to 50 ms to reach it. The required ordering and deadlines can conflict; the item also independently requires transmission after safe-state entry.
findings.requested_change: Resolve the report ordering and deadlines with the product owner, and state mutually achievable conditions.

findings.description: The item treats every watchdog reset as a detected fault. SYS-SUP-022, SYS-SUP-023 and SYS-SUP-042 then require a safe-state reaction and supervisor reset, potentially causing repeated resets after a watchdog reset. CON-SUP-111 requires classification and CON-SUP-112 names code 8, but neither specifies this recovery loop.
findings.requested_change: Clarify the intended reporting and recovery behavior for a watchdog reset with the product owner, and specify how it interacts with the fault reaction.

findings.description: CON-SUP-112 defines the timestamp as milliseconds since start without identifying the start reference; OP-SYS-001 records this uncertainty. The allowed entity values also do not identify an appropriate entity for watchdog reset code 8.
findings.requested_change: Obtain and specify the timestamp reference and the entity value for watchdog reset reports.

findings.description: CON-SUP-113 and the requirement name the response field <state> but do not define its possible values or their meanings. A verifier cannot determine the correct status response.
findings.requested_change: Obtain and specify the permitted state values and their mapping to controller states.

findings.description: The requirement says to return the last 8 fault reports but does not specify the response when fewer than eight faults are retained. CON-SUP-113 also leaves this case unspecified.
findings.requested_change: Obtain and specify the response for fewer than eight retained reports, including an empty history.

findings.description: The requirement unconditionally requests a software reset after entering the safe state, whereas STK-SUP-010 and CON-SUP-110 require the controller to remain in the safe state until power-on when the repeated-fault latch applies. CON-SUP-115 also requires a configuration fault to latch the safe state.
findings.requested_change: Specify the reset request conditions and exceptions consistently with the agreed safe-state latch behavior.

findings.description: The requirement detects an overrun when execution has not completed at limit expiry. CON-SUP-103 describes an overrun as execution longer than the limit, but also requires detection when the limit expires; the treatment of completion exactly at the limit is unresolved.
findings.requested_change: Resolve the boundary case and align the detection rule with the product-owner decision.

findings.description: Health depends on whether a flow fault has been detected for a task, but CON-SUP-104 and SYS-SUP-006 define a flow fault for the cycle without specifying how it is attributed to a task. Watchdog refresh eligibility after a flow fault therefore has no unique interpretation.
findings.requested_change: Define how a flow fault affects task health or define watchdog refresh eligibility directly for a flow fault.

findings.description: Health depends on whether a flow fault has been detected for a task, but CON-SUP-104 and SYS-SUP-006 define a flow fault for the cycle without specifying how it is attributed to a task. Watchdog refresh eligibility after a flow fault therefore has no unique interpretation.
findings.requested_change: Define how a flow fault affects task health or define watchdog refresh eligibility directly for a flow fault.

findings.description: The requirement calls for an application-image integrity check, but CON-SUP-107 does not define the image check method or reference data. A test cannot determine the expected outcome for a given image.
findings.requested_change: Specify the approved image integrity method and reference data so the check has an objective pass criterion.

findings.description: CON-SUP-107 specifies the CRC polynomial but not the other CRC parameters or the covered byte range. The stated test cannot determine a unique expected CRC for a configuration block.
findings.requested_change: Specify the complete approved CRC parameters, covered bytes and stored-value representation.

findings.description: CON-SUP-110 places fault-report transmission after safe-state entry and before the reset request. This item specifies only the latter ordering; OP-SYS-008 records the unresolved interaction with the report and safe-state deadlines.
findings.requested_change: Resolve the ordering and deadline interaction and state the approved relationship between safe-state entry, report transmission and reset request.

findings.description: The item treats each watchdog reset as a detected fault, which invokes the general fault reaction in SYS-SUP-022, SYS-SUP-023 and SYS-SUP-042. CON-SUP-111 and CON-SUP-112 do not establish whether that reaction is intended for code 8; its report entity is also undefined.
findings.requested_change: Define the approved reporting and recovery behavior for watchdog resets, including the code 8 entity.

findings.description: CON-SUP-113 specifies the STS response format but does not define the permitted <state> values or their mapping to controller states. A test cannot determine the correct response value.
findings.requested_change: Specify the approved state values and their mapping to controller states.

findings.description: The phrase "refresh ... only while" restricts when refreshes may occur but does not require a refresh or specify its frequency. A controller that never refreshes the independent watchdog could satisfy this wording, despite the 100 ms timeout in CON-SUP-106 and the servicing intent in STK-SUP-005.
findings.requested_change: Specify when or how often the independent watchdog must be refreshed during fault-free operation, using the supported timeout and identifying any missing input needed to define the rule.

findings.description: SYS-SUP-010 bounds only the time between consecutive refreshes; it does not bound the first refresh after control cycles begin. CON-SUP-106 specifies a 100 ms timeout, so the watchdog could reset before that first refresh. OP-SYS-004 records that watchdog servicing during start-up and meeting the timeout in that phase are undecided.
findings.requested_change: Define the first refresh deadline relative to watchdog activation or the preceding start-up refresh, consistent with the decided start-up servicing behavior.

findings.description: CON-SUP-112 specifies a timestamp in milliseconds since start but does not identify the start reference, so the timestamp in SYS-SUP-032 is ambiguous.
findings.requested_change: Define the timestamp reference and update the requirement after the product owner decides it.

findings.description: CON-SUP-112 permits a task name, CODE or CONFIG as the report entity, but none identifies the watchdog reset represented by code 8.
findings.requested_change: Define the report entity for watchdog reset code 8 after the product owner decides it.

findings.description: CON-SUP-103 calls execution longer than the limit an overrun while requiring detection at expiry. SYS-SUP-004 leaves the treatment of completion exactly at the limit unresolved.
findings.requested_change: Resolve the equality boundary and state a consistent detection rule.

findings.description: SYS-SUP-014 requires an application-image integrity check, but CON-SUP-107 does not define its method or reference data, so a test cannot determine the expected outcome for a given image.
findings.requested_change: Define the image integrity method and reference data after the product owner decides them.

findings.description: CON-SUP-107 specifies the CRC polynomial but not the other CRC parameters or the covered byte range, so SYS-SUP-016 does not determine a unique expected CRC.
findings.requested_change: Supply a complete CRC definition and covered data range.

findings.description: CON-SUP-110 places fault-report transmission after safe-state entry and before reset; SYS-SUP-026 specifies only the latter ordering. SYS-SUP-032 also imposes a 10 ms reporting deadline while safe-state entry may take up to 50 ms.
findings.requested_change: Resolve the ordering and deadlines with the product owner and specify consistent obligations for report transmission.

findings.description: SYS-SUP-031 treats each watchdog reset as a detected fault, invoking the general fault reaction and reset request. CON-SUP-111 and CON-SUP-112 do not establish whether that reaction is intended for code 8.
findings.requested_change: Decide and specify the reporting and recovery behavior after a watchdog reset.

findings.description: CON-SUP-113 and SYS-SUP-034 do not define the permitted STS state values or their mapping to controller states, so the correct response cannot be determined.
findings.requested_change: Define the state values and their mapping after the product owner decides them.

findings.description: SYS-SUP-010 bounds the interval between consecutive refreshes but does not bound the first refresh after control cycles begin. CON-SUP-106 specifies a 100 ms timeout, so the watchdog may reset before the first refresh.
findings.requested_change: Specify a first-refresh deadline consistent with the watchdog timeout and the decided start-up servicing behavior.

findings.description: CON-SUP-111 requires the reset cause to be readable by the service tool. SYS-SUP-029 and SYS-SUP-030 classify and transmit it at start-up, but no requirement provides service-tool access to the cause.
findings.requested_change: Specify how the service tool reads the classified reset cause, including the applicable interface behavior.

findings.description: CON-SUP-115 requires an out-of-range configuration fault at start-up to latch the safe state. SYS-SUP-009 detects the fault and SYS-SUP-042 refers to such a latch, but no requirement actually requires it to be set.
findings.requested_change: Add the required safe-state latch behavior for the start-up configuration fault.

findings.description: SYS-SUP-035 specifies GET FAULTS only when at least eight reports are retained. CON-SUP-113 requires the service response, but behavior with fewer retained reports is unresolved.
findings.requested_change: Specify the response for fewer than eight retained reports, including an empty history, after the product owner decides it.

findings.description: CON-SUP-104 requires checkpoints of tasks released in a control cycle by its end, while CON-SUP-103 permits T_DIAG to execute for 20 ms in a 10 ms cycle. SYS-SUP-006 applies the cycle-end rule and SYS-SUP-007 excludes T_DIAG from its explicit missing-checkpoint rule.
findings.requested_change: Resolve the T_DIAG checkpoint timing and update the flow requirements consistently.
